title: Tenali Raman Tale 94

full_text:
An ambassador from the court of Isfahan arrived in Vijayanagara, presenting three philosophical riddles to King Krishnadevaraya:
'First: Where is the exact center of the earth?
Second: How many stars shine in the heavens?
Third: What is the exact difference between a wise man and a fool?'

The court scholars attempted complex mathematical calculations of spheres and constellations, but none could satisfy the foreign envoy.
Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, I shall answer the ambassador’s questions immediately.'

Tenali took an iron peg and a mallet. He walked to the exact center of the palace audience hall, drove the peg firmly into the floor tiles, and announced:
'Here, noble envoy, is the exact center of the earth!
If you doubt my calculation, take your measuring ropes and measure the earth in all four directions. If it is off by even an inch, I will surrender my head!'
The envoy smiled wryly, unable to measure the planet.

For the second question, Tenali brought a fat, woolly mountain ram into the hall.
Tenali pointed to the ram’s dense, curly fleece:
'There are precisely as many stars in the heavens as there are hairs upon the body of this ram!
If you do not believe me, count the hairs on this ram, and then count the stars in the sky. If the counts differ by a single hair, my answer is void!'
The envoy laughed, recognizing the impossible parallel.

For the third question, Tenali asked: 'What is the difference between a wise man and a fool?'
Tenali pointed to the court:
'A wise man knows when he does not know, and remains silent to observe and learn.
A fool pretends to know everything, asking unanswerable questions to trap others, while remaining blind to the truth before his feet!'

The Persian envoy was enchanted by Tenali’s brilliant philosophical agility.
He bowed low, presented Tenali with a chest of Persian carpets and rosewater, declaring that Vijayanagara possessed the sharpest intellect in the Orient.
moral: Cosmic riddles are solved through the profound geometry of human existence.
